text:
Where I could not be honest,
I never yet was valiant.
plain: I won't be brave about anything I can't be honest about.
You do not choose when you arrive or when you leave. What counts is being ready.

text:
We are not the first
Who with best meaning have incurr’d the worst.
plain: Meaning well does not protect you from the worst. Plenty of good people have been hit hard.

text:
The gods are just, and of our pleasant vices
Make instruments to plague us:
plain: Your own indulgences become the tools that bring you down. Pleasure has a bill.

text:
Thou hast spoken right, ’tis true;
The wheel is come full circle; I am here.
plain: What you do comes around. The wheel always makes a full turn.

text:
Why should a dog, a horse, a rat have life,
And thou no breath at all? Thou’lt come no more,
Never, never, never, never, never!
plain: Why do a dog and a rat get to live and she does not. Grief doesn't come with an answer.

text:
The weight of this sad time we must obey;
Speak what we feel, not what we ought to say.
The oldest hath borne most; we that are young
Shall never see so much, nor live so long.
plain: In hard times, say what you actually feel, not what you are supposed to say.

text:
Let fame, that all hunt after in their lives,
Live registered upon our brazen tombs,
And then grace us in the disgrace of death;
When, spite of cormorant devouring time,
Th’ endeavour of this present breath may buy
That honour which shall bate his scythe’s keen edge,
And make us heirs of all eternity.
plain: Everyone chases fame. Make your effort count now, so that time cannot cut it down later.

text:
The mind shall banquet, though the body pine.
Fat paunches have lean pates, and dainty bits
Make rich the ribs, but bankrupt quite the wits.
plain: Let the body go hungry if it feeds the mind. Overindulged people end up with thin brains.

text:
Why, all delights are vain, but that most vain
Which, with pain purchased, doth inherit pain:
plain: All pleasures are empty, but the emptiest are the ones you pay for in pain.

text:
Too much to know is to know naught but fame,
And every godfather can give a name.
plain: Knowing the names of things is not knowing things. Collecting facts is not understanding.

text:
So study evermore is overshot.
While it doth study to have what it would,
It doth forget to do the thing it should;
And when it hath the thing it hunteth most,
’Tis won as towns with fire: so won, so lost.
plain: We chase what we want so hard we forget what we should do, and then it burns down as soon as we get it.

text:
Necessity will make us all forsworn
Three thousand times within this three years’ space;
For every man with his affects is born,
Not by might mastered, but by special grace.
plain: Everyone is born with urges that willpower alone does not beat. Expect to fail some, and plan for it.

text: And therefore welcome the sour cup of prosperity! Affliction may one day smile again, and till then, sit thee down, sorrow.
plain: Take the bitter days with a straight face. Hard times do turn, so let sorrow sit for now.

text: Why, will shall break it; will, and nothing else.
plain: A vow only holds as long as your will does. Willpower is the only thing that keeps it.

text: Imitari is nothing: so doth the hound his master, the ape his keeper, the tired horse his rider.
plain: Copying is nothing. The hound copies the master, the ape copies the keeper, the tired horse copies the rider.

text:
Sowed cockle reaped no corn,
And justice always whirls in equal measure.
plain: Plant weeds and you get no corn. What you put in is what you get out.

text: That is the way to make an offence gracious, though few have the grace to do it.
plain: The way to make a mistake look fine is to own it with confidence, but few have the nerve.

text: Great reason, for past cure is still past care.
plain: What cannot be fixed should not be carried. Past cure, past care.

text: And so may you, for a light heart lives long.
plain: A light heart lives long. Do not carry more weight than the day requires.

text:
The blood of youth burns not with such excess
As gravity’s revolt to wantonness.
plain: Nothing burns hotter than a serious, disciplined person who suddenly cuts loose. Watch for it in yourself.

text:
Henceforth my wooing mind shall be expressed
In russet yeas and honest kersey noes.
plain: From now on I speak in plain yeses and honest noes. No fancy phrases.

text: A heavy heart bears not a nimble tongue.
plain: When you are weighed down, you do not have clever words. Do not push for them.

text: Honest plain words best pierce the ear of grief;
plain: When someone is hurting, plain honest words get through where fancy ones do not.

text:
Fair is foul, and foul is fair:
Hover through the fog and filthy air.
plain: Nothing is what it looks like. Good and bad trade places in the fog.

text:
Nothing in his life
Became him like the leaving it; he died
As one that had been studied in his death,
To throw away the dearest thing he ow’d
As ’twere a careless trifle.
plain: He faced his end like he had rehearsed it, as if his life were a small thing to give. How you leave says a lot.

text:
There’s no art
To find the mind’s construction in the face:
plain: You cannot read a person's real mind from their face. Trust is a bet.

text:
And oftentimes to win us to our harm,
The instruments of darkness tell us truths;
Win us with honest trifles, to betray’s
In deepest consequence.
plain: Dark forces will tell you something true to lure you into something terrible. A small win can be bait.

text:
Present fears
Are less than horrible imaginings.
plain: What you imagine is almost always worse than what is really in front of you.

text:
Come what come may,
Time and the hour runs through the roughest day.
plain: Whatever comes, the day ends. Time moves through even the worst ones.

text:
To beguile the time,
Look like the time; bear welcome in your eye,
Your hand, your tongue: look like the innocent flower,
But be the serpent under’t.
plain: Your face is a book anyone can read. Control it, because people read you before you speak.

text:
If it were done when ’tis done, then ’twere well
It were done quickly.
plain: If you are going to do something, do it fast. Dragging it out only makes it worse.

text:
We still have judgement here; that we but teach
Bloody instructions, which being taught, return
To plague th’ inventor.
plain: Whatever harm you teach, you teach it to the one who comes back for you. The same hand takes the poison.

text:
We will proceed no further in this business:
He hath honour’d me of late; and I have bought
Golden opinions from all sorts of people,
Which would be worn now in their newest gloss,
Not cast aside so soon.
plain: You earn a good name by effort, and it is worth wearing while it is fresh. Do not throw it away.

text:
I dare do all that may become a man;
Who dares do more is none.
plain: There is a line to what makes you a man. Go past it and you are something else.

text:
But screw your courage to the sticking-place,
And we’ll not fail.
plain: Tighten your nerve all the way and you will not fail. Commit fully.

text:
Merciful powers,
Restrain in me the cursed thoughts that nature
Gives way to in repose!
plain: Even good people have dark thoughts when they are tired or alone. Ask for help holding them off.

text:
Sleep that knits up the ravell’d sleave of care,
The death of each day’s life, sore labour’s bath,
Balm of hurt minds, great nature’s second course,
Chief nourisher in life’s feast.
plain: Sleep repairs what the day wears down. Do not treat it as optional.

text:
The sleeping and the dead
Are but as pictures. ’Tis the eye of childhood
That fears a painted devil.
plain: Your fear is often a child scared of a painted devil. Look at it plainly.

text: The labour we delight in physics pain.
plain: Work you love takes the sting out of pain.

text:
There’s nothing serious in mortality.
All is but toys: renown and grace is dead;
The wine of life is drawn, and the mere lees
Is left this vault to brag of.
plain: Once the thing that gave life its weight is gone, everything else is a toy.

text:
Th’ expedition of my violent love
Outrun the pauser, reason.
plain: When emotion runs hot, it outpaces the part of you that says wait.

text:
To show an unfelt sorrow is an office
Which the false man does easy.
plain: Anyone who is faking can fake sorrow easily. Real feeling does not need a show.

text:
There’s daggers in men’s smiles: the near in blood,
The nearer bloody.
plain: The closer someone is to you, the more harm they can do. Watch who smiles.
